taste.name: No-Shadow Flat Depth
taste.trigger: When deciding how pricing cards, feature panels, and code-screenshot mockups should read as distinct surfaces
taste.decision: Chose zero elevation shadows, using near-invisible background tint instead, over conventional card shadows
taste.reason: A product about AI agents doing real engineering work wants to feel calm and technical, not like a marketing site stacking glossy cards
evidence: card-detection heuristic (shadow-or-border required) found zero matches anywhere

taste.name: Single-Typeface, Weight-Only Hierarchy
taste.trigger: Differentiating an 80px hero headline from 17.5px body copy and 14.5px button labels
taste.decision: Chose one variable font (Google Sans Flex) across every role using fractional weights (300/400/450/500), over pairing a display face with a separate body face
taste.reason: A single voice at every scale feels engineered and consistent — appropriate when the product itself, not the marketing copy, is meant to be the star
evidence: uniqueFamilies = Google Sans Flex + icon font only, on all 3 pages
weightDistribution never exceeds 500 on any page

taste.name: Accent Color Confined to Its One Job
taste.trigger: Deciding where the system's one non-neutral hue (#3279F9 blue) should appear
taste.decision: Chose to restrict blue to /pricing alone (a promo link + plan-tier badges), over extending it as a site-wide accent
taste.reason: Color pulls attention; the only place a user needs a quick visual distinction is comparing pricing tiers — everywhere else it would compete with product screenshots
evidence: absent from home and /product top-6 color lists entirely

taste.name: Decorative Motion Stays Out of the UI's Way
taste.trigger: Wanting a distinctive 'liftoff' mood without making the interface feel unpredictable
taste.decision: Chose to split motion into page-specific atmospheric particle fields versus one shared functional hover transition, over a single unified animation system
taste.reason: Users get the brand personality without it ever slowing down or obscuring what they came to click
evidence: particle pattern differs per page (arc on /product, confetti on /pricing)
identical 'transform 0.3s ease-in-out, background-color 0.3s' hover transition string on all 3 pages
